llm_justification.summary: A sharp upward move in the implied probability that Israel strikes 4+ countries in 2026 is a signal of expected broadening Middle East military conflict. The cleanest liquid proxy is crude oil (geopolitical risk premium, up), with defense/aerospace equities a weaker secondary (up). Both mappings are modest-confidence: oil can move meaningfully only on a concrete escalation headline, and 12h magnitudes frequently stay below the 700bps tradable threshold. If the probability spike is speculative or already-public, expect little or reversing follow-through.
key_assumptions: A rising probability reflects genuinely higher expected regional escalation, not resolution-criteria technicalities
Escalation would threaten energy supply/transit enough to add a crude risk premium
The information is not already fully reflected in oil and defense prices
failure_modes: Escalation is anticipated/already public, so assets have already priced it and do not move further
The probability move is noise or low-liquidity, with no real-world escalation following
Oil fails to respond because spare capacity/weak demand caps the risk premium despite escalation
Broad risk-off dominates, pulling oil and even defense ETFs down intraday
Strikes counted by this market (e.g., on non-oil-producing neighbors) have minimal energy-market relevance, making the proxy weakly exposed
